items.title: Marriott’s Fees Jump 14% as Hotel Owners Seek a Bigger Cut
items.summary: Marriott said that its talks with hotel owners who want a bigger cut of the pie have been "constructive." It's easier for everyone to stay polite about the fee math when profit growth has revived significantly.

items.title: Chinese Embassy Warning Knocks Thailand’s China Rebound
items.summary: Golden Week gave Thailand its first real sign that Chinese travelers were coming back. Now a single embassy advisory has put that at risk, and Lunar New Year 2027, coming in early February, will show whether the damage is a dip or something more prolonged.

items.title: Ryanair Warns of Pay Freezes and Labor Unrest as Fuel Costs Surge
items.summary: Even with a strong balance sheet, Ryanair is squeezing pay and hiring as its cheap fuel hedges run out. If the strongest airline in Europe is bracing for a difficult 2027, weaker rivals face a much harder winter.

items.title: Inside the Unraveling of the Tollman Family Travel Dynasty
items.summary: The company was doing fine. The family wasn’t.

items.title: War Insurance Dries Up for Gulf Events as U.S.-Iran Conflict Continues
items.summary: Gulf events can still insure against cancellation but not against war. That is pushing organizers to postpone events or to take on the risk themselves. It’s a growing issue, and Saudi Arabia’s calendar has been paying the price.

items.title: Flying Around Russia Is Testing Airlines’ Climate Targets
items.summary: Avoiding Russia has become a climate problem for airlines heading from Europe to Northeast Asia — and a competitive disadvantage. Finnair, one of the most affected airlines, says it’s committed to its climate goals.
